content_sections.heading: About JNCASR
content_sections.text: JNCASR is an autonomous research institution under the Department of Science and Technology, Government of India, and a Deemed to be University. It is located at Jakkur P.O., Bengaluru - 560064, Karnataka. The Medical Officers will work at its campus healthcare facilities in Bengaluru under the Chief Medical Officer.

content_sections.heading: JNCASR Medical Officer Vacancy Details 2026
content_sections.text: The amount above applies to candidates other than pensioners. Personnel retired from Central or State Government service and drawing pension receive a fixed monthly remuneration as per the applicable Government norms, arrived at by deducting the gross basic pension from the pay drawn at retirement. No increment or Dearness Allowance is admissible during the contract. Remuneration commences from the date of reporting for duty at the place of posting. content_sections.heading: JNCASR Medical Officer Eligibility 2026
content_sections.text: The candidate should not be more than 60 years of age as on the last date of submission of the application. The engagement is subject to the condition that the candidate shall not continue beyond the age of 65 years. M.B.B.S. degree from a recognized Institute/University specialized in General Practice. Minimum 5 years of post-internship experience as a Medical Officer/Medical Practitioner in a reputed hospital, medical centre, healthcare facility, or medical centre of a reputed educational/research institution. Preference will be given to candidates with experience of providing medical services in an educational/research institution, autonomous institution, or similar campus-based healthcare facility. JNCASR functions in a computerized environment, so the appointee is expected to possess basic computer skills. The official notification carries the complete eligibility conditions for this post.

content_sections.heading: Selection Process
content_sections.text: Applications received will be scrutinized. Only shortlisted candidates will be called for interview. Candidates fulfilling the eligibility conditions shall be considered on relevant criteria such as qualification, experience, suitability and other requirements of the Centre. A Committee shall be constituted for the purpose of selection.

content_sections.heading: Service Conditions
content_sections.text: The appointment is purely contractual, for one year from the date of joining or until the candidate attains the age of 65 years, whichever is earlier. It may be extended after the first year, subject to satisfactory performance, review and functional requirements of the Centre. Either side may terminate the appointment at any time by giving 30 days' notice. The Centre may instead pay one month's remuneration in lieu of notice, without assigning any reason, including where performance or discharge of duties is not found satisfactory by the Competent Authority. The place of duty is Dhanvantari, JNCASR, Main Campus, Jakkur, and allied facilities in Bengaluru, namely Sahyadri Campus, Chamundi Campus and Arkavathi Campus. Normal duty is in general shift (9.00 AM to 2.00 PM or 2.00 PM to 6.00 PM) every day. Appointees are on call during nights and provide weekend coverage (9.00 AM to 2.00 PM or 2.00 PM to 6.00 PM). Attendance must be marked online. Appointees perform the duties assigned by the Competent Authority and work under the Chief Medical Officer (CMO). Other duties may be assigned as and when required, with no extra or additional allowance. Only basic facilities and infrastructure required for the assigned duties are provided. No transport facility or telephone/internet facility at the residence is provided. There is no entitlement to Provident Fund, Pension, Gratuity, Medical Attendance/Treatment, Seniority, Promotion or other benefits available to regular Government servants. The appointee has no claim or right to regular appointment to any post under the Centre. The Centre is not responsible for any loss, accident, damage or injury arising out of or in connection with the assigned work, including related travel. On appointment, the appointee must take an oath of allegiance to the Constitution of India or make a solemn affirmation in the prescribed proforma. The contract and its continuation are governed exclusively by the stated terms and conditions, as amended from time to time.

faq.question: Q1. Can a retired government doctor apply?
faq.answer: Yes, if the age and other eligibility conditions are met. A retired Central or State Government doctor drawing pension is paid a fixed monthly amount worked out by deducting the gross basic pension from the pay drawn at retirement.

faq.question: Q2. Does experience in a campus clinic help?
faq.answer: Yes. Preference goes to candidates who have provided medical services in an educational or research institution, an autonomous institution, or a similar campus-based healthcare facility.

faq.question: Q3. Will the job involve night or weekend duty?
faq.answer: Yes. Appointees are on call at night and provide weekend coverage in the 9.00 AM to 2.00 PM or 2.00 PM to 6.00 PM slots.

faq.question: Q4. Will all applicants be called for interview?
faq.answer: No. Applications are scrutinized first, and only shortlisted candidates are called.

faq.question: Q5. How much paid leave will a Medical Officer get?
faq.answer: Paid leave is allowed at 1.5 days for each completed month of service, and unused leave cannot be carried beyond a calendar year.

faq.question: Q6. Can the contract end before one year?
faq.answer: Yes. Either side can end it with 30 days' notice, or the Centre can pay one month's remuneration instead of notice.

faq.question: Q7. Is a late application accepted?
faq.answer: No. An application received after 5:00 p.m. on the closing date shall not be considered.

faq.question: Q8. Which campuses can a Medical Officer be posted to?
faq.answer: Duty is at Dhanvantari on the Jakkur Main Campus and at the allied Sahyadri, Chamundi and Arkavathi campuses in Bengaluru.
